questions.title: In the rational exponent expression x^(a/b), what does the denominator 'b' represent?
choices: The index of the radical root
questions.explain: The denominator of a fractional exponent always represents the root index, while the numerator represents the power.

questions.title: Convert the radical expression ⁵√y³ (fifth root of y cubed) to its rational exponent form.
questions.explain: According to the root‑to‑exponent rules, the power (3) becomes the numerator, and the index (5) becomes the denominator, giving y^(3/5).

questions.title: How is the expression x^(1/4) represented in radical form?
choices: The square root of x cubed
The reciprocal of x to the fourth power
questions.explain: An exponent of 1/4 means the power is 1 and the root index is 4, which is written as the fourth root of x.

questions.title: Evaluate the numerical expression: 27^(2/3).
questions.explain: First take the cube root of 27 (which is 3), then square that result: 3² = 9.

questions.title: Evaluate the numerical expression: 16^(3/4).
questions.explain: First take the fourth root of 16 (which is 2), then raise that result to the third power: 2³ = 8.

questions.title: Evaluate the expression: (-32)^(3/5).
questions.explain: First take the fifth root of -32 (which is -2 since (-2)⁵ = -32), then raise -2 to the third power: (-2)³ = -8.

questions.title: Evaluate the expression: (-16)^(1/2) in the real number system.
questions.explain: An exponent of 1/2 represents a square root. In the real number system, the square root of a negative number is undefined.

questions.title: Evaluate the negative rational exponent expression: 8^(-4/3).
questions.explain: The negative exponent tells us to take the reciprocal: 1 / [8^(4/3)]. Since the cube root of 8 is 2, and 2⁴ = 16, the result is 1/16.

questions.title: Which of the following radical representations is equivalent to the exponential expression x^(1/2)?
questions.explain: A rational exponent of 1/2 represents the principal square root of the base, written as √x.

questions.title: Rewrite the radical expression ³√a⁷ (cube root of a to the seventh power) in exponential form.
questions.explain: The power inside is 7 (numerator) and the root index outside is 3 (denominator), which translates directly to a^(7/3).
